tagline: Across the northern tier, from the Allegheny to Pine Creek.
intro: Out of Warren, US 6 winds south into the Allegheny National Forest through Clarendon and Sheffield, then swings east across the northern tier through Kane, Mount Jewett, Smethport, Port Allegany and Coudersport. Past Denton Hill it takes up Pine Creek and follows it down through Galeton to Ansonia, then runs on by way of Wellsboro to Mansfield.
Counting its extensions and offsets it is 211 miles, the longest scenic byway in Pennsylvania by far, and every one of the 34 municipalities along it passed a resolution in support.

moments.title: Kinzua Bridge
moments.text: A tornado in 2003 brought down 11 of the old railroad viaduct's 20 spans, and the Skywalk now runs 600 feet out on the towers left standing, above the wreck where it fell.

moments.title: Pennsylvania Lumber Museum
moments.text: Below Denton Hill the museum keeps logging locomotives and sawmill machinery from the late 1800s, along with forester Bob Webber's cabin, moved intact out of Pine Creek Gorge.

moments.title: Ansonia
moments.text: Here Pine Creek leaves the road and turns south into its gorge, a course it took about 20,000 years ago when the retreating glacier dammed its old way northeast.
